title: Number Quest Unit 6 · The Building Yard (Explorer)

misconceptions: thought 3 sides were enough
correct
thought any shape with corners counts
thought any shape with more sides counts
items.why: Quadrilateral means 4 straight sides. A rectangle has 4; a triangle has 3, a pentagon 5 and a hexagon 6.

items.q: You face the door, then make a quarter turn. How big an angle did you turn?
misconceptions: thought a turn is not an angle
mixed up a quarter turn with a whole turn
thought a quarter turn is smaller than a square corner
correct
items.why: An angle is an amount of turn. A quarter turn is exactly one square corner, the turn at every corner of a rectangle.

items.q: A square is a kind of rectangle. Why is that true?
choices: It is bigger than other rectangles
It has 4 sides and 4 square corners, like every rectangle
It has 4 equal sides, and rectangles never do
misconceptions: sorted by size instead of by properties
correct
thought a rectangle can never have 4 equal sides
sorted by names instead of by properties
items.why: A family is decided by properties. Every rectangle has 4 sides and 4 square corners, and a square has both, so a square belongs in the rectangle family.

items.q: A garden is 6 meters long and 4 meters wide. What is its area?
misconceptions: found the fence instead of the carpet
added the sides instead of multiplying
correct
multiplied and then added the sides too
items.why: Area is the carpet: multiply the sides. 6 × 4 = 24 square meters. (Adding around the edge, 20, would give the perimeter.)

items.q: A square painting has sides of 5 inches. What is its perimeter?
misconceptions: counted only two of the four sides
counted only three of the four sides
found the carpet instead of the fence
correct
items.why: Perimeter walks all the way around: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 inches. (25 would be the area, the squares inside.)

items.q: A rug is 8 feet long and 3 feet wide. Which pair is right?
misconceptions: swapped the fence and the carpet
counted only half the fence
correct
added the sides for the carpet instead of multiplying
items.why: Fence first: 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22 feet of perimeter. Carpet second: 8 × 3 = 24 square feet of area.

items.q: Two roads on a map run side by side and never cross. What kind of lines are they?
misconceptions: mixed up parallel and perpendicular
correct
mixed up a ray with a pair of lines
missed that the roads are straight
items.why: Lines that run side by side and never meet are parallel. Perpendicular lines are the ones that cross at a square corner.

items.q: Which letter folds exactly in half, both sides matching?
misconceptions: missed that the arms of F point one way only
missed that the open side of G has no match
correct
missed that the hook of J has no match
items.why: The letter A folds along a line down its middle: the two halves match exactly. F, G and J have parts with nothing to fold onto.

items.q: A treasure hides at the point (4, 2) on a grid. Starting at (0, 0), how do you walk to it?
misconceptions: swapped the two numbers in the address
correct
walked down instead of up
added the two numbers together
items.why: In a grid address, the first number counts steps right and the second counts steps up: (4, 2) is 4 right, then 2 up.
